title: The Tool Modules
objective: Understand how lib/*.cjs modules organize GSD's functionality into domains

content.value:
GSD's real work happens in library modules under get-shit-done/bin/lib/. Each module owns one domain:

  core.cjs    — Shared utilities, output/error, path helpers
  config.cjs  — Config file CRUD, model resolution
  phase.cjs   — Phase directory lifecycle
  state.cjs   — STATE.md reading and writing
  roadmap.cjs — ROADMAP.md parsing and updates
  verify.cjs  — Verification and validation
  commands.cjs — Git commits, compound operations
Every module follows the same pattern: 'use strict', require Node built-ins first, then require local modules, define functions, export at the bottom.

Notice the two kinds of functions:

1. cmd* functions (like cmdConfigEnsureSection) — called from the dispatch switch. They handle args, call output() or error(), and always exit the process.

2. Internal functions (like loadConfig) — called by other modules. They return values normally. Some are suffixed with 'Internal' to signal they are not meant for external use.

The output() function is GSD's standard exit path. Every successful command calls output() which writes to stdout and exits with code 0. Every failure calls error() which writes to stderr and exits with code 1. There is no other way to end a command.

successCriteria: You can explain the difference between cmd* functions and internal functions, and describe how output() and error() work
